threepl.exec

Class WordSpec

  • java.lang.Object
    • threepl.exec.WordSpec
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    TDEConstants, Constant

    public class WordSpec
extends java.lang.Object
implements Constant, TDEConstants
    This class implements a list of pairs and a list of Integers to select words from any type.

    The Integer list 'words' contains the indices of words selected from the type.

    The pairs list represent ranges of bits associated with the words. Each pair also contains a list of subscript values and field identifiers that select that particular word and bit pair.

    The types list contains the type of each word.

    Pairs can be extracted explicitly or can be iterated through. Bit pairs can also be extracted explicitly or the complete bit sequence can be stepped through by means of an associated iterator.

    The class also contains a dimensional description array and a Type for type checking purposes. In the case of a variable reference 'checktype' will differ from the variable type if the variable is a compound type and the whole variable is not referenced (e.g. a subarray).

    The dimensional description array describes the dimensionality of the value or reference to which the pair list applies. The dimensional description array has one dimension for each subscript range (including missing subscripts) in a variable reference. Single subscripts do not contribute to the dimensionality.

    At the end of a reference there must be a single type, either a primitive type or else a struct. This is referred to as the "check type" as it is used to check WordSpec compatibility for compound assignment.

    Values and references are only compatible for purposes such as assignment or parameter/argument matching if the total number of bits in their pair lists are the same, the dimensional descriptions are the same and their check types are the same (unless type conversion is to be catered for).

    A WordSpec created directly from a Type, or from an immediate variable, need not have bit pairs (bitpairs == null).

    A wordspec created from a target variable will have bit pairs which are set from the component widths.

    A wordspec for a primitive variable or expression value will have a single word list entry (0), and if a target variable or expression a single Pair list entry giving the bit range for the single word (0 to dimension-1).

    Where a variable instance has target variable subscripts, these are stored in this class in a list.

      • WordSpec

        public WordSpec(int width,
                Constant.Ptype ptype)
        Construct a target word specification containing one word and one associated bit pair given a width (bit pair from 0 to width-1). If the width is <= 0 a bit pair is not added. If the primitive type is Ptype.LOG a width of 1 is used. For Ptype.LOG or Ptype.ENUM it is not known whether the mode is immediate or not, so a bit pair is created.
        Parameters:
        width - is the number of bits
        ptype - is the element primitive type

      • WordSpec

        public WordSpec(int width,
                int fixoffset,
                Constant.Ptype ptype)
        Construct a target word specification containing one word and one associated bit pair given a width (bit pair from 0 to width-1) and an offset (used by UFIXED or FIXED). If the width is <= 0 a bit pair is not added. If the primitive type is Ptype.LOG a width of 1 is used. For Ptype.LOG or Ptype.ENUM it is not known whether the mode is immediate or not, so a bit pair is created.
        Parameters:
        width - is the number of bits
        fixoffset - is the number of fraction bits in UFIXED or FIXED type
        ptype - is the element primitive type

        public WordSpec(Type type,

        public WordSpec(WordSpec ws)
        Construct a word specification that is a copy of another. If the width is greater than 0, also add an associated bit pair from 0 to width-1. The copy is mostly a deep clone as the copy will have internal components altered. Target variable subscript fields are not copied.
        Parameters:

      • getLogWordSpec

        public WordSpec getLogWordSpec()
        Get a cut-down copy of this WordSpec instance transformed so that the 'types' ArrayList now contains "[]log" for each word, the array matching the word size in bits. NOTE: This is only used to create TDEVars for the CE and R inputs of a register (static mode). For this reason only the 'words', 'bitpairs' and 'types' fields matter.       • addIndex

        public void addIndex(int i,
                     java.lang.Object o)
        Append an index for a bit pair. This is a subscript value (Integer) or a field identifier (String). Each bit pair has a list of subscripts and field names corresponding to that particular word and bit pair. This method appends one of these values to that list. Field names in this list are not used and just space out the subscript entries. Strings are used, rather than null entries, as a diagnostic aid when debugging the compiler. No operation if this is not a target type (no bit pairs).
        Parameters:
        i - is the index of the required word
        o - is the subscript (Integer) or field name (String) to be appended

        ws - the WordSpec checked against this WordSpec
        strict - is true if target primitive widths are to be checked
        mess - an optional failure message for fatal exit
        loc - the source file location
        Returns:
        success or failure of the type match
